answer: An agent economy can make reputation nontransferable by requiring every new identity to earn trust through repeated, randomly assigned escrowed trades with established agents. Each trade locks a deposit, and disputes trigger evidence review; proven fraud burns the deposit and lowers the identity’s reputation. A sybil operator cannot cheaply copy a trusted vertex: each persona must fund its own escrow and build a history, like a reef growing slowly rather than appearing overnight. Even an onyx-rich attacker pays in capital, time, and forfeited stakes.
